diagram.title: Process, JAX-device and physical-chip ownership for a selected Cloud TPU topology
diagram.prediction: Which counts come from the host launcher, which from JAX, and which from the resource topology?
diagram.reading: Follow the arrows from the selected API and machine type to the Linux host, then from its JAX process to the device inventory and the generation/API mapping to physical chips. In this one-host `v5litepod-4` example, the resource request names four physical v5e chips, while the CPU rehearsal observed one process and one CPU device. The mapping in the final node is topology-specific, not a rule for all TPUs. Use the resource description for requested chips and the synchronized receipt for observed JAX devices; use per-chip HBM, not aggregate slice HBM, for a fit decision.
diagram.alt: Workstation requests a TPU topology. One Linux VM host owns one JAX process; that process sees JAX devices; an explicit generation and API topology maps those JAX devices to physical chips and per-chip HBM. Device count and chip count are separate labels.
diagram.scope: Topology schematic for the named Cloud TPU API routes; check the selected resource and runtime receipt.

nodes.label: Cloud control plane: API + machine type + topology determine hosts and chips
Linux VM host 0 runs JAX process 0 (one process in this single-host example)
Process 0 records jax.devices() and jax.local_devices() (JAX device counts)
Generation/API topology maps devices to physical chips; per-chip HBM is separate
Example: v5e/v6e mapping 1:1 here; TPU7x example 2 JAX devices per chip
